Implement GitHub issue #145: "Add descriptions to categories" in this repo (expense-tracker).

## Goal
Add an optional free-text `description` to a category that states what kind of expense belongs in it. It must be settable/editable/clearable in the UI, carried through the API, fed into the AI category-selection prompt, and exposed over MCP.

## Acceptance criteria (must all hold)
- A user can set, edit and clear a category description, with the length limit enforced and a clear validation error shown.
- Existing categories keep working with no description (the column is nullable; a blank description is stored as absent/NULL).
- The AI category-selection prompt includes each category's description when present; covered by a test using the fake Bedrock client (no external calls).
- `list_categories` (MCP) exposes the description.
- All category queries stay scoped by `user_id`.

## Scope and design decisions (already decided, follow exactly)

### Data + API
- New nullable `description` column on the `category` table via a new evolution file `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/17.sql` (highest existing is 16.sql). App-level validation only: no DB CHECK constraint and no column DEFAULT for the business rule.
- Limit: description trimmed, max 500 characters; blank -> stored as absent (NULL).
- Thread `description` through the Tapir request/response models in `lib/api/shared` (these already exist: `CreateCategory`, `UpdateCategory`, `GetCategories` under `.../api/models/categories/`). Endpoint definitions stay in `lib/api/shared`, never in `server/`.
- Update `CategoryDAO` (`server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/CategoryDAO.scala`) and the corresponding action(s): parser, INSERT, UPDATE, SELECT. Keep every query user-scoped (`WHERE user_id = ?`) and every list query with a stable `ORDER BY`.
- Use Chimney `transformInto` for case-class shape mapping where applicable, matching existing style.

### Validated field (important)
- Introduce a validated primitive `CategoryDescription` in `lib/common/shared` with a `TextValidator`, mirroring how existing primitives like `Name`/`Email`/`Password` are defined and validated. The 500-char/trim/blank-is-absent rule lives in that validator and is shared by the API and the web form (no duplicate ad-hoc checks). If a `CategoryName` validated primitive does not already exist, prefer reusing whatever the category name currently uses rather than inventing a parallel one; do not change the existing name semantics.

### Web form (important)
- Convert ONLY the category create + edit form on `CategoriesPage` (`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/CategoriesPage.scala`) to the template's typed-form pattern: a `FormData[Request]` built from `FormField[T: TextValidator]`, driven by `StatefulFormData`. Use the existing library types from package `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.forms` (`FormData`, `FormField`, `StatefulFormData`). The canonical in-repo templates to copy are `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/UpdateInfoFormData.scala` together with `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/widgets/EditUserForm.scala` (and `SignInForm.scala`). Create a new `CategoryFormData` in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/` holding the name and description fields and producing the create/update request via `submitRequest`.
- Do NOT touch the other places categories get created on the fly (the free-solo autocomplete category creation in the expense/refund/import-rule forms, and the create-category modal on `MerchantsPage`). Those are autocomplete flows that do not fit `FormField`. For those, only make sure the new `description` field flows through the shared API models; do not refactor them to `FormData`.
- Show the description as helper text where a category is picked, only where it fits without clutter.
- Frontend reachability: the create/edit form is already reachable on `CategoriesPage`; no new route is needed. Confirm the edited form still renders and is reachable.

### AI
- When a category has a description, include it in the category-selection prompt built in `StatementSuggestionsService`. If the JEV variant (`JevStatementSuggestionsService`) also selects categories by name, include it there too. Add/extend a test using the existing fake Bedrock client to assert the description appears in the prompt when present. No external API calls in tests.

### MCP
- `list_categories` must return the description. Update `McpTools`/`McpDispatcher` and the MCP tests accordingly.

## Tests
- Add/update server tests (testcontainers Postgres + fakes) for: DAO/action round-trip of description, validation rejecting an over-limit description with a clear error, blank-stored-as-absent, the AI prompt including descriptions (fake Bedrock), and MCP `list_categories` exposing it.
- Add/update a web test for the converted `CategoriesPage` form if the existing test conventions cover it (see `docs/guide/testing.md`); component tests use `BrowserRouter` + jsdom.

## Hard constraints (repo is PUBLIC)
- The PR title, body and all commit messages must contain NO PII: no real bank names, account numbers/last4, real filenames, merchant names, or amounts. Use placeholders.
- Do NOT put any claude.ai session link in commits or the PR. `Co-Authored-By` lines are fine.
- Custom wart `NamedArguments`: when a call has 2+ arguments of the same type they MUST be passed by name or it fails to compile.
- No silent defaults for missing data: validation fails loudly with a clear error; never fabricate a value.

## If the code differs from this spec
If something in the codebase does not match what is described above (different field names, an existing validated primitive, a different suggestions-prompt structure, etc.), adapt to the actual code rather than forcing the spec, keep the acceptance criteria intact, and document each such deviation in a short "Spec deviations" section of the PR description.
